question: Can a timing-independent compiler policy plus serial speculative GDN replay produce a cold, fresh-cache, target-exact static-MTP1 lane above 50 tok/s without GPU compile faults?
control: MTP0 R15 with W8A16, deterministic Inductor, XPU Graph off, persistent GDN state, explicit oneCCL Work.wait, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, max-autotune=0, and coordinate-descent-tuning=0.
candidate: The simplified R46 static-MTP1 image: R31 userspace plus only the pinned R35 serial-GDN kernel binaries; identical compiler policy to the control; packed RMSNorm serial exact and native speculative GDN serial exact enabled.

sequence: Run one MTP0 control and one MTP1 candidate. If and only if every workload/canary gate passes, all 12 outputs match, no GPU fault occurs, and candidate throughput exceeds 50 tok/s, run a second fresh-cache control and candidate and require the complete four-arm cross-product to be exact.
promotion_gate: All four fresh-cache attempts must pass; each same-profile repeat and every MTP1-to-MTP0 comparison must match 12/12 complete token arrays; the MTP1 two-attempt class-balanced median must exceed 50 tok/s; kernel logs must remain clean. Otherwise the lane remains unqualified.
reporting: No favorable-cache selection, no output tolerance, no shortened suite, and no performance promotion or external submission before the complete gate passes.
